back.description:
What the person brings back of what they dropped in earlier rounds, by id, with their words on how; empty
words bring it back as it was. Only the person brings back.

context.description: The person's own words for the agents that work after this answer. It changes no verdict.

shown.description: The fingerprint of the question the answerer was shown.

verdicts.description: A verdict per item id. An item left out is kept.

Aspect.description: One part of an item, shown apart: its label and what it is, in plain words.

By.description: Who gave an answer, and under which authority.

oneOf.description: The person, from the page or a channel only they hold.
A rule in code, by its name.
An agent or any other program.

about.description: What the check holds the output to. For an open check the agent reads it before it delivers.

reads.description:
Earlier steps the check reads besides what its step uses, such as the hidden cases a proof runs. Only a
hidden check may read a hidden step.

oneOf.description:
The agent knows it before it delivers, and a failure goes back to the same session to be fixed in place:
the form of the output (a field, a length, a file that must exist), or the project's own tests, which the
agent can run itself.

Proof the maker never sees: not its name, not its inputs. A failure tells the agent only the check's own
sentence, and spends the attempt.
Failed. `reasons` is what the agent is told; `detail` and `cases` only the person sees.

cases.description: The hidden cases that failed, each in full: never told to the agent (G3).

oneOf.description: The check could not judge at all, such as a tool it runs that did not start: Jaynes's fault.
Merged by Jaynes, never pushed, and undone by the person with Undo.

Digest.description: The fingerprint of some content. Two contents have the same digest only if they are equal.

Effect.description: What the step does to the world, by where its effect lands.

oneOf.description:
Nothing that stays changed outside the step's own output. What a step sends in a request is a flow, the
matter of its reach and not of its effect, so a step whose network only reads has this effect.
Changes only Jaynes's copies, which are thrown away or kept by Jaynes.
Changes something real that a named operation undoes, such as a local merge.
Cannot be undone: a push, a message to a person, a publication.
An agent program, such as Claude Code, does the step.
The role program does the step itself, for evidence an agent could fake.
The person: the step is a question over the steps it needs, and its output is the answer.

FailedCase.description:
A hidden case that failed, as the check ran it, for the person: what it says, the command it ran, the code it
exited with (0 is what it expects) and the end of what it printed.

Given.description: An earlier step's output given to a call.

delivery.description:
How the run delivers on a repository: a branch, or a merge into the branch the project had checked out when
the run started.

protocol.description: The major version of the protocol the role speaks.

target.description: What the run works on. A role that names none works on a repository, as every role did before targets.

oneOf.description: The agent program's tools that read the web, such as Claude Code's WebFetch and WebSearch.

Only the registries packages are installed from (npm, Go modules, PyPI, crates), from the step's commands:
the step installs what the project needs, and reaches nothing else.

Offer.description: What a stop may let the person grant with their answer, beside their verdicts: only the person, never an agent.

oneOf.description:
The project's tests start their own test servers on ports the system picks, as `jaynes project test-servers
DIR` lets them: never the ports of the usual databases and caches, which only that command lets, naming them.

Offers.description: What a stop offers the person to grant, and the field of its step's output that marks each beforehand.

marked_by.description: For an offer, the boolean field of the step's output that marks it beforehand; one not named starts unmarked.

Photo.description: The window a page is photographed in, in CSS pixels, and whether down to its last line when taller.

Rate.description: A rate in (0, 1), compared by its bits so a role stays comparable.

Reach.description: What a step may reach. Jaynes turns it into the agent program's own settings for the step.

commands.description: Whether the step may run shell commands.

local_ports.description:
The local ports the step's commands may connect to, such as a service on this machine the step acts on. A
port is reached only when it is named here: none is open by default.

write.description: Project paths a writing step may change; `!` keeps paths out.

required.description: Features without which the role cannot run.

schema.description: The JSON Schema the output must follow, shown to the agent.

oneOf.description: The output of a role's own step.
A role's own step asks the person something before it can give its output.
The step cannot be done, for a reason of the role's.
The role could not answer the call at all: the engine counts it as its own fault, never the agent's.

extensions.description: Room to grow: anything a later version adds before it has a field of its own.

oneOf.description: Write the instructions for an agent's attempt at a step.

checks.description: The step's open checks, which the agent knows.

oneOf.description: Do a step of the role's own.

any_port.description:
The person opened this project's checks to every local port (`jaynes project open-ports`), as the run's
setup recorded it when it started: the role's box then lets its commands reach any local TCP port. Left
out when not.

freed_ports.description:
With `test_servers`, the ports of the usual databases and caches that macOS's box holds while the commands
run which the person let this project's tests use (`jaynes project test-servers DIR PORT`): never held, and
bound and reached as a step's own. Left out when none.

key.description: For a step that cannot be undone: pass it to the service that acts, so a repeat counts once.

project.description: The run's copy of the project, for a step that reaches it.

source.description: The person's own folder the run started from, never to be written.

test_servers.description:
The person let this project's tests start their own test servers (`jaynes project test-servers`), as the
run's setup recorded it or the person chose since: macOS's box then lets its commands serve on a port the
system picks, and reach the window of ports the system gives next. Left out when not.

any_port.description:
The person opened this project's checks to every local port (`jaynes project open-ports`), as the run's
setup recorded it when it started: the role's box then lets its commands reach any local TCP port. Left
out when not.

freed_ports.description:
With `test_servers`, the ports of the usual databases and caches that macOS's box holds while the commands
run which the person let this project's tests use (`jaynes project test-servers DIR PORT`): never held, and
bound and reached as a step's own. Left out when none.

project.description:
For a step that reaches the project: the files of the project as Jaynes measured them when the attempt
ended, and as the delivery carries them, laid out in a folder of their own beside the run's copy, with no
repository and with the copy's installed dependencies linked in; never the run's copy itself. What git
ignores is not there. The folder goes when the check is over.

start.description:
The project as the run began, for a check that compares with it: the engine's repository beside the
run's copy, out of every agent's reach, and the commit the run began from. Given by the engine from the
run's copy, never read from where `project` is, the state judged laid out apart. Left out when not known.

test_servers.description:
The person let this project's tests start their own test servers (`jaynes project test-servers`), as the
run's setup recorded it or the person chose since: macOS's box then lets its commands serve on a port the
system picks, and reach the window of ports the system gives next. Left out when not.

oneOf.description: What the person is shown of an output: one item per thing they may judge.

The output with only the items the person chose, each as it was: a stop that chooses asks for it when the
person chose without a note, so no agent works. The reply is a `result`.
A small change that can be undone: the short path.
Anything else: the full path.

ShownItem.description: An item as the role lists it. The engine computes its fingerprint from `content`.

aspects.description:
The parts of the item the person judges apart, each with its label, such as an option's palette and fonts.
Shown, and read with the person's words; the engine judges the item as a whole.

detail.description: A few plain sentences shown under the label.

photo.description: How a page among the pictures is photographed: its window, and whether whole. None: a computer's window.

pictures.description:
Pictures of the item: files in the step's copy of the project, by path from its root. Jaynes keeps a copy of
each, by its fingerprint, so what the person sees never changes under them.

Start.description: Where the project stood when the run began: a repository and a commit of it.

attempts.description: Attempts the agent may spend in one round. Only the agent's faults spend one.

delivered.description:
Whether what the step writes is part of what the run delivers. false: the step draws only for the person to
choose from (identity's boards); its paths, the step's `reach.write`, stay in the run's tree, where later steps
and their checks read them, and in the run's record and on its page, and never go into the delivery.

fixes.description: Times a failed shape check goes back to the same agent session to be fixed in place, per attempt.

from_risk.description: The lowest risk at which the step runs: a step from `high` is left out of the short path.

hidden.description: Proof the maker never sees: the step reads only the request, and no agent step reads it.

idempotent.description:
Doing the step's act again does no harm (the far side keeps the act's key, or the act sets a state rather than
adding one): only then may Jaynes start it again after a fault, with the same key. Any step that acts, whatever
can undo it; for an effect that cannot be undone it may also be said inside the effect, as before.

model.description:
The size of model the step's agent works with: "small" for a step that needs less (fix-bug's cases). The
engine maps it to a model of the run's agent; a role never names one.

session.description: Whether an agent step goes on in the session of the agent step before it, so one agent holds several steps.

turns.description:
At most this many turns of the agent's model in one attempt, after which it delivers what it has; none, no
cap but the agent program's own.

StepModel.description: The size of model a step's agent works with.

oneOf.description: The run's own model.
A smaller model of the run's agent, which the engine names.

answers.description:
The role's words for its verdicts at this stop, such as "Yes" for keep and "No, it's something else" for redo:
the person reads them on the buttons, and what each one does is still said by Jaynes under it. A verdict
the role names no word for keeps Jaynes's name. Empty: every verdict keeps it.

audit_rate.description: The share of runs a certified stop still asks.

budget.description: The error rate the stop may have once it asks only a sample. None: it always asks.

choose.description:
The person chooses one of the step's options with a click, and may write how to adjust it. The others leave
the running; without a note the run goes on with the chosen one alone, kept by Jaynes and not the agent.

from_risk.description: The lowest risk at which the stop asks.

holds.description: Whether the steps after it wait for the answer. Otherwise the run goes on and the answer corrects it later.

note.description:
A line of the role's under the question, said before the person looks, such as "The layout of your screens
comes later." at a stop that keeps only colours and fonts. Empty: nothing is said.

offers.description:
What the person may grant with their answer at this stop, such as the project's test servers at the first stop
of a new project: only the person, and only while the stop is open.

redo.description:
The earlier step whose work this stop asks about, when the step that asks only reviews it: what the person
sends back goes to that step, and this one looks again at what comes back before the person sees it.

release.description:
The stop only asks whether a result may go on, not a matter of taste or direction: an agent may let it
go on, recorded as the agent's, and the person can still change that.

rounds.description:
Kept so roles that set it still load; it limits nothing. Every round at a stop is opened by an answer of
the person, who decides when to stop, so no count of them is a ceiling. Agents redoing without a new answer
are what a ceiling guards against, and a step's attempts and fixes already are that ceiling: when they are
spent the run is blocked and calls the person, never ended.

verdicts.description: The verdicts the person may give each item, from the closed list.

Target.description:
What a run works on, and so what it delivers, what its reach is given in, how its risk is judged and how its
delivery is undone. One engine for every kind: the core's rules are the same, only these readings change.

oneOf.description:
A repository: the run works in a clone of it at the commit it had, its reach is given in the repository's
paths, its risk is judged by the lines and files it changes, and it delivers a branch, or a merge that Undo
reverts.

VerdictKind.description: The closed list of verdicts on an item.

oneOf.description: Keep the item as it is. A later round may not change it.
Change it as the person writes.
Have the step do it again, with the person's note.
Drop it for good: it does not come back in the run.
"I don't know": leave it as the agent made it, unjudged.
